title: 1980 AHSME Problem 29
statement: How many ordered triples \((x,y,z)\) of integers satisfy the system of equations below? \[ \begin{aligned} x^2-3xy+2y^2-z^2&=31,\\ -x^2+6yz+2z^2&=44,\\ x^2+xy+8z^2&=100. \end{aligned} \]

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: a finite number greater than two

solutions.text:
Adding the three equations gives \[ \begin{aligned} x^2-2xy+2y^2 &{}+6yz+9z^2\\ &=175, \end{aligned} \] or \[ (x-y)^2+(y+3z)^2=175. \] A square is congruent to \(0\) or \(1\pmod4,\) so a sum of two squares cannot be congruent to \(3\pmod4.\) But \(175\equiv3\pmod4,\) a contradiction. Thus there are no integer triples.

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Add all three equations before trying to solve for the variables
Rewrite the resulting quadratic form as a sum of two squares and reduce modulo \(4\)
